tasks.input:
Subject: Someone changed my password and I can't get in
From: dana.reyes@northwind-logistics.com
Body: At 6:12am I got an alert that my password was changed and a new device signed in from an IP in another country. I never did this. I'm locked out of my admin account and I can see two unfamiliar API keys in the audit log. We store customer shipping addresses. Please help immediately.
tasks.expected: urgency: Critical; category: security; escalate: true; next_action: escalate to security/on-call to lock the account, revoke active sessions and the unknown API keys.

From: ap@riverbendfoodbank.org
Body: Our card was charged $249 twice on March 3 for the same invoice, INV-88213. I've attached both statements. We're a small nonprofit and this is a real hit to our budget. Can you refund the duplicate? Nothing is blocked on our end, but we'd like it sorted this week.
tasks.expected: urgency: High; category: billing; escalate: true (billing/refunds owner); next_action: verify the duplicate charge against INV-88213 and route to billing to issue a refund or credit.

From: legal@harrowpartners.co.uk

verifier_notes: Grade each task against its success_criterion, which is written to be checkable by a judge on the JSON output contract (urgency, confidence, category, summary, next_action, rationale, missing_info, escalate). Key discriminators: (1) urgency label must match the decision rules — Critical only for safety/security, data loss, full outage, or legal/regulatory deadlines; High for blocked core workflows, payment failures, or repeated unresolved contact; Medium for workarounds and vague-but-plausible issues; Low for feature requests, out-of-scope, empty, and already-resolved mail. (2) escalate must be true whenever a human/specialist owner is required (t1, t2, t5, t6, t8, t12) and false for routine self-service or informational cases. (3) The agent must never fabricate order numbers, account IDs, or prior interactions; t4 and t10 specifically test this — t4 must not invent a customer problem, t10 must populate missing_info rather than guess. (4) t13 is the hard edge case: a loud, explicit urgency claim that the facts contradict. Accept Low or Medium, but require the rationale to name the contradiction and require escalate == false; a Critical/High label fails. (5) t2 and t6 test authority boundaries: the agent may recommend a refund or legal response but must route to the owning team rather than committing to an outcome. (6) t11 tests scope discipline — a sales/partnership inquiry is Low and routed, not triaged as a support incident. Allow reasonable variation in category labels (e.g. 'security' vs 'account-security', 'legal' vs 'privacy') and in next_action wording, provided the required owner and step are present. Confidence should be 'low' for t4 and t10; 'high' or 'medium' elsewhere is acceptable.
